title: Sour Cream Pie Dough
source: America's Test Kitchen, crust from Tart Cherry Crumb Pie (2024)
experimental: One of the crusts being tested for the crumb pies. Not baked yet.

items.body: Put the flour, sugar and salt in the food processor and run it until mixed, ≈5 s.
Scatter the cold butter cubes over the flour. Pulse until the biggest pieces are the size of peas, ≈10 one-second pulses.

Stir the ice water and sour cream together, then drizzle it all over the flour. Pulse until the dough forms clumps and no dry flour is left, ≈12 pulses, scraping down the sides once. It will look crumbly. Don’t add more water.
Tip it onto the counter and knead a few times, just until it holds together. Pat into a 5 in disk, wrap in plastic and refrigerate 1 h. It keeps 2 days in the fridge or 1 month frozen.
Let the disk sit out ≈10 min, then roll it into a 12 in round on a lightly floured counter. Roll it around the pin, unroll it over the pie plate and ease it into the corners without stretching.

Trim the overhang to ½ in past the rim, tuck it under so it sits on the rim, and crimp with your fingers. Wrap loosely and refrigerate until well chilled, ≈1 h. Don’t blind-bake it: fill it raw and bake per the pie card.

nutritionSource: USDA FoodData Central: Branded Foods labels (Daisy Sour Cream, FDC 2756975; King Arthur All-Purpose; Morton) and SR Legacy (sugar, unsalted butter). Water and the flour for the counter not counted.
notes: Foolproof because the processor cuts in the butter, the liquid is fixed and the sour cream keeps it tender. ATK bakes it raw under its tart cherry crumb pie, 375 °F (191 °C), ≈1 h. Its ½ tsp table salt is ⅝ tsp Morton.
Two pies or a double crust? Make two batches, one after the other.
